$comment: ONE number, read by TWO gates, and that is the whole point of the file.
check-plan-housekeeping.sh DEMANDS that a plan older than delete_days be
deleted. check_plan_boxes.py's A5 (not yet built) REFUSES to delete a plan
that still carries open boxes -- unless it is older than delete_days.
Those two predicates are complements over this single number, so their
permitted sets are disjoint by construction and no plan can ever be in both.
Duplicating `33` into two scripts is exactly what would create the deadlock:
a 34-day-old plan with one open box would be simultaneously must-delete and
must-not-delete, and no commit would satisfy both. So neither gate may inline
the number, and both name this file in their manifest `leaves`.
AGE IS CONTENT AGE, not 'last commit touching the path'. The difference is
load-bearing: a plan moved into the archive would otherwise reset its clock,
which makes archiving a way to cheat the age gate. Because the archive is
append-only, an archived plan's blob never changes and its clock keeps
ticking -- so it ages out on schedule and archiving buys nothing.
warn_days exists because this gate is clock-driven: its verdict can flip
overnight with no commit, which scripts/lib/suppression-liveness.ts normally
bans. The warn band is what makes that exception humane -- a plan announces
the date it will go red about a week before it does.
